prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Companion Trait"]
1: ["Customize Pet Stance & Desktop Dock Location", "Select how your pet appears on your primary desktop monitor.", "Confirm & Proceed"]
2: ["1. Drag pet across screen\n2. Right click for system menu\n3. Press Alt+P to hide"]
3: ["Meet Your Desktop Companion", "Your virtual pet lives right on your desktop while you work and play."]
4: ["Your pet will appear in the bottom-right corner of your primary display."]
5: ["Sign In to Sync Your Existing Pet", "Logging in connects your cloud save so your existing companion profiles and items are restored automatically.", "Use your original email to recover previously adopted pets."]
6: ["For best results, use clear lighting without heavy shadows or obstructed faces.", "Lighting Tip"]
7: ["Claim Your Exclusive Starter Pet Toy", "Complete setup now to unlock the Golden Ball pet accessory directly in your tray!", "Free Starter Gift Included"]
8: ["Look for the pet icon in your system tray to manage settings anytime."]
9: ["Official Companion Adoption Badge"]

verdicts.problem: Mentions free gifts and creates urgency around completing setup
